Repo: H:\Kasirku (Next.js 16 App Router POS/accounting SaaS "Kasirku"). I need factual research (not implementation) on the CURRENT state of 5 different areas, to scope 5 separate feature requests just given by the project owner. Report facts with file:line references for each numbered area below — don't recommend solutions yet, I'll design those myself afterward.

### 1. Product categories
Look at `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/products/` (product management). Is "category" currently a free-text field on each product (e.g. a plain text column, autocomplete-from-existing-values), or is there a dedicated `categories` table/management UI where categories must be created first and products then pick from a fixed list? Show the add/edit product form's category input specifically (file + relevant JSX/logic). Also check the `products` table schema (grep migrations for `create table.*products` or `alter table products.*category`) to see the actual column type/constraint.

### 2. Kitchen printer category routing + POS category filter
I already know `kitchen_printers.categories text[]` exists (routes kitchen tickets to printers by category — built earlier). Question: is there any UI in Settings' add-printer-form.tsx or elsewhere that already lets you visually pick "which categories route to this printer" (I recall checkboxes for this — confirm). Separately: does the actual POS/kasir screen (`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx`) have ANY existing category filter/tabs for the product grid (e.g. buttons to filter by category when browsing products to add to cart), or does it just show ALL products in one flat list/grid with just a search box? Show the relevant product-grid rendering code.

### 3. Zero-stock selling
Find where stock is checked before allowing a product to be added to cart or checked out in `pos-screen.tsx` (search for `stock` comparisons, disabled states based on stock, "Stok habis"/"sold out" logic). Show the exact conditions that currently block adding/selling a zero-stock item.

### 4. Void transaction PIN requirement
Find the void transaction flow(s): search for `void_transaction`, `owner_void_transaction`, and any void-related form/button in `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/` (I know `void-transaction-form.tsx` exists). Show its current logic — does it currently ask for ANY PIN/password confirmation before voiding, or does it just immediately call a server action with no extra confirmation, when accessed from the web dashboard (owner's authenticated session)? Also check `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts` or wherever `owner_void_transaction`/`void_transaction` RPCs are actually called from, and whether there's a SEPARATE cashier-initiated void path anywhere (e.g. from the POS screen itself, not just the dashboard transaction detail page) that might already require a cashier PIN.

### 5. Manual transaction entry — date vs time, and page layout
Show `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/new/manual-transaction-form.tsx` and `new/page.tsx` in full — specifically the date input (is it `type="date"` only, no time component?) and the `create_manual_transaction` RPC/action signature (does it accept a full timestamp or just a date?). Also confirm the current `transactions/page.tsx` layout structure (I know it has "Ekspor CSV"/"+ Tambah Transaksi Manual" buttons plus an inline "Impor dari CSV" card both stacked above the transaction list on the SAME page — just confirm this is still accurate) so I can plan splitting import/manual-entry into a separate area.

Report concisely per numbered section, code excerpts + file:line only, no recommendations.

content.text:
## 1. Product categories

**Free text, no dedicated table.** `category` is a plain nullable `text` column with no FK/enum/check constraint.

- Schema: `H:\Kasirku\supabase\migrations\20260702100200_products_ingredients_recipes.sql:7` — `category text,` inside `create table public.products (...)` (line 3).
- Add form: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\products\add-product-form.tsx:84-93` — plain `<input id="category" name="category" type="text" placeholder="mis. Minuman" />`. No datalist/autocomplete, no select.
- Edit form: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\products\edit-product-form.tsx:126-132` — same, a controlled `<input type="text">`.
- Server action just trims and stores the raw string, `null` if empty: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\products\actions.ts:16` (add) and `:97` (edit), written via `category: category || null` at lines 54 and 130.
- CSV import also writes raw category strings straight from the CSV cell with no validation against existing values: `actions.ts:325` (`const category = get("category") || null;`).
- The only place distinct category values are computed anywhere in the app is a one-off `Array.from(new Set(...))` query built for the kitchen-printer form (see #2), not a managed categories table: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\settings\page.tsx:104-112`.

## 2. Kitchen printer category routing + POS category filter

**Printer form: yes, checkboxes exist.** `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\settings\add-printer-form.tsx:200-217` renders one checkbox per distinct product category (`name="categories" value={c}`), only shown `{categories.length > 0 && (...)}`. The `categories` prop is the caller-computed distinct list from `products.category` (not a real categories table): `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\settings\page.tsx:94, 104-112, 228` (`<AddPrinterForm action={boundAddKitchenPrinter} categories={productCategories} />`). Table column confirmed elsewhere: `kitchen_printers.categories` in `supabase/migrations/20260702100500_fnb_support_tables.sql`.

**POS screen: no category filter, flat grid + search only.** Confirmed by grep — `category` appears exactly once in `pos-screen.tsx`, only as a `Product` type field (`H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\pos\pos-screen.tsx:29`), never used for filtering/tabs/UI.

- Only filter mechanism is the search box + Enter-to-scan: `pos-screen.tsx:192-201` (`filteredProducts` filters by `name`/`barcode`/`sku` substring match only) and `:240-252` (barcode/SKU exact-match on Enter).
- Product grid rendering (flat, no category grouping/tabs): `pos-screen.tsx:933-987` — a single `<div className="grid grid-cols-2 ... sm:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4">` (`:941`) iterating `productGroups.map(...)` (`:942`), where `productGroups` (`:205-216`) groups only by product **name** (for variants), not by category.
- Search input itself: `pos-screen.tsx:884-891` (`placeholder="Cari produk atau scan barcode…"`).

## 3. Zero-stock selling

Client-side blocking happens in two places in `pos-screen.tsx`:

- `addToCart(product)` — `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\pos\pos-screen.tsx:273-296`: if the product is already in the cart, blocks incrementing when `existing.qty >= product.stock` (`:277`); if not yet in cart, blocks entirely when `product.stock <= 0` (`:282`, silently returns `prev` — no cart entry, no error message).
- Product grid button `disabled` prop — `pos-screen.tsx:950, 955`: `soldOut = isVariantGroup ? totalStock <= 0 : single.stock <= 0` (`:950`), then `disabled={soldOut || (!isVariantGroup && inCart >= single.stock)}` (`:955`). Label switches to `"Stok habis"` at `:970-972` when `soldOut`.
- Variant picker buttons — `pos-screen.tsx:1004, 1012`: `const soldOut = v.stock <= 0;` then `disabled={soldOut || inCart >= v.stock}`, label `"Stok habis"` at `:1020`.
- Cart qty stepper `+` button is also capped: `disabled={item.qty >= item.maxStock}` at `:1085`.
- `changeQty` clamps to `Math.min(i.maxStock, ...)` at `:309`, so qty can never exceed on-hand stock via the stepper either.

No server-side stock check exists in `pos-screen.tsx`/`actions.ts` — checkout is delegated entirely to the `checkout_transaction` Postgres RPC (`H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\pos\actions.ts:69-109`, RPC call at `:92`), so any stock enforcement beyond the client-side blocks above lives in that DB function, not in the TS action.

## 4. Void transaction PIN requirement

**Dashboard void (regular transactions): no PIN/password, immediate RPC call.**

- `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\transactions\[transactionId]\void-transaction-form.tsx`: only a reason `<select>` (`VOID_REASONS` at lines 7-13, rendered `:67-78`) plus a "Void Sekarang" confirm button (`:85-91`). No PIN/password field anywhere in the file. `handleConfirm` (`:41-53`) calls `ownerVoidTransaction(businessId, transactionId, invoiceNumber, reason)` directly (`:44`) with no extra confirmation step.
- Server action `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\transactions\[transactionId]\actions.ts:9-37` (`ownerVoidTransaction`) calls RPC `owner_void_transaction` (`:16-20`) with `p_business_id`, `p_transaction_id`, `p_reason` only — no PIN parameter passed at all. It relies purely on the caller's authenticated Supabase session (owner dashboard auth).

**Separate cashier/manager-PIN-gated void path exists, but for a different transaction type ("ticket" transactions), not the main POS flow:**

- `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\ticket-reports\[transactionId]\void-ticket-transaction-form.tsx` has a PIN input: `id="voidPin" type="password" inputMode="numeric" maxLength={6}` (`:75-84`), labeled "PIN Manajer" (`:72-74`), with submit disabled until `pin.length >= 4` (`:93`).
- It calls `voidTicketTransaction(businessId, transactionId, pin, reason)` (`:35`) from `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\pos\ticket-actions.ts:123-137`, which passes `p_manager_pin: managerPin` to RPC `void_ticket_transaction` (`:131-137`) — the PIN is verified server-side inside that RPC.
- This is not reachable from `pos-screen.tsx` (the main retail/F&B cart screen) — it's reached only from the ticket-reports section (`ticket-reports/[transactionId]/`), which is a separate feature for ticket-based sales (see `ticket-pos-screen.tsx`). No void button/flow exists inside `pos-screen.tsx` itself — grep for `void` in that file and in `pos/actions.ts` returns nothing.

## 5. Manual transaction entry — date vs time, and page layout

**Date input is `type="date"` only, no time field.**

- `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\transactions\new\manual-transaction-form.tsx:131-138`: `<input id="txn-date" type="date" value={date} max={todayDateString()} onChange={...} />`.
- On submit, the date string is converted with a hardcoded noon time before being sent: `manual-transaction-form.tsx:105` — `new Date(\`${date}T12:00:00\`).toISOString()`. So whatever time of day the sale actually happened is not captured; every manual transaction is stored at 12:00:00 local (Asia/Jakarta, per `todayDateString()` at `:26-28`) unless a different hour is derived elsewhere (it isn't).
- The RPC signature does accept a full timestamp, not just a date: `H:\Kasirku\supabase\migrations\20260725120000_manual_transactions.sql:11-18` — `create or replace function public.create_manual_transaction(p_business_id uuid, p_date timestamptz, p_items jsonb, p_payment_method text, p_received numeric default null, p_customer_id uuid default null)`. Grant statement confirms type: `:196` — `... (uuid, timestamptz, jsonb, text, numeric, uuid) ...`. So the DB layer supports a real timestamp; only the UI/client forces it to noon.
- Server action passthrough: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\transactions\new\actions.ts:12-19` (`createManualTransaction(businessId, date, items, paymentMethod, received, customerId)`) forwards `date` straight to `p_date` in the RPC call (`:26-33`) with no server-side date/time manipulation.
- `page.tsx` (`H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\transactions\new\page.tsx`) is a plain server component fetching `products`/`customers`/`customPaymentMethodRows` and rendering `<ManualTransactionForm ... />` (`:62-67`) — no date/time logic there.

**`transactions/page.tsx` layout — confirmed as described:**

- `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\transactions\page.tsx:58` renders `<TransactionButtons businessId={businessId} />` (contains "⬇️ Ekspor CSV" link and "+ Tambah Transaksi Manual" link — defined in `transaction-actions.tsx:11-30`, lines 20 and 26 respectively) directly above `:61` `<TransactionImportCard importAction={boundImportTransactions} />` (an inline card titled "Impor dari CSV", defined in `transaction-actions.tsx:32-56`, heading at `:44`), both stacked above the transaction list `<div className="mt-6 space-y-2">` at `:63` — all on the same page, same component tree, no separate route.
- Both `TransactionButtons` and `TransactionImportCard` are hidden on native (Capacitor) builds: `transaction-actions.tsx:12` and `:40` (`if (Capacitor.isNativePlatform()) return null;`).
